steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Er, excuse me, who are ye... sir?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Phew... much better.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Once you reach a certain age, you come to prefer bright and warm places.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: And... is that beans I smell?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Er, aye, I was cookin' some canned beans for dinner...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: D'ye want some, sir?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Don't mind if I do.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Would be better if we had some seasoning from home, perhaps some marinated meat.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Aye, I was thinkin' the same! We Gododdins...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I ken who ye are now, and ye’re a wee bit different from whit’s in the news.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Ah. Well, you can ask your captain. I held her when she was wee.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Little Rita touched my horn and asked why her dad didn't have one.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: ...I apologize for my insolence at the time, Your Grace.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Not many have the nerve to touch my horns, Lieutenant Skamandros. You showed courage from a very young age.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Or should I say... all of you are brave warriors of Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Your defense of Chetleigh was outstanding, as was your performance at Brentwood.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: The Exemplars, you call yourselves...

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: I've long wanted to meet you, though it seems your leader does not welcome my presence.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Pardon my frankness, Your Grace, but it is hard to treat your sudden appearance as a pure gesture of good faith.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Of course, Lady Windermere. I understand.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Especially in times like this.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: I sent men to the Irnclad Galavae. They were traveling quickly, but fortunately, I made it in time to present funeral flowers for Amphelise.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: ...I appreciate the gesture.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I assume the duke of Gododdin hasn't come all the way here just to give us a medal?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: What if I say I have?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Most of us are neither nobles nor intelligentsia. It would be best if you didn't beat around the bush.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Your Royal Highness Alexandrina is as direct as they say.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Or would you prefer that I called you 'Siege', like your friends do?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: I fully understand why the Exemplars avoided the ducal armies along the way.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: You didn't want them to get involved in the machinations of the dukes.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: You want to fight only for Victoria and her people, like the legendary unit that you're named after.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: And so, I'm not here as the Duke of Gododdin.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: I'm here as Sean Gododdin, Member of Parliament, to extend an invitation to the Parliament authorized Tempest Platoon and the rest of the Exemplars.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Leave that outdated identification code behind. I'm asking that you intervene in this war in the name of Parliament.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: The miners' camp has burned to the ground.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: No sign of Sarkaz soldiers.
Misery feels a slight chill. The campsite’s charred debris has cooled.
He moves some collapsed wooden beams aside, and finds a few unrecognizable bodies.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Miners. Remains of the Infected.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: It's all the same, everywhere.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: What's that sound?

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Nice hiding spot, Sudaram.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Nachzehrer spotted to the northwest of Gibsonham—

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Out of comms range already?

steps.name: Sudaram
steps.text: Death has you.
Several rune swords pierce out of the ground beneath Misery's feet, but he is no longer there.
Misery rips through the fabric of space with his dagger and retreats out of range. The collapsed ruins turn into a cage, trapping the Nachzehrer's withered bodies.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Shush now...

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: I have you too.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...Duke Gododdin.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I understand that the Victorian Parliament has not held a session for a long time.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Everyone who escaped Londinium knows that the Sarkaz have been the ones giving the orders from the Palace of Westhaleg during this time.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Of course. I don't deny the present circumstances.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Why don't we cast our gaze further, though, to the future beyond the war?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The future? Isn't it a little too early to be bargaining over that — if 'bargaining' and 'coercion' were synonyms?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: You misunderstand me. Gododdin is not Caster. I would much prefer to sit by the fireside than gather at the negotiation table. I'm more about drinking and playing cards with friends.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: It gets cold rather quickly once summer is gone. Mind if I have my men add some wood to the fire?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You might as well have them come in.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: That's much better.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Where were we? Oh yes, the future.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: We know that the war will end, and Victoria will triumph.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: The war will inevitably bring... or should I say has already brought about irreversible changes, ending a twenty-year stalemate.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If anyone in the room is interested in the empty throne, it certainly isn't me.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Excellent, excellent! See? We already have a consensus.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: As a matter of fact, I held a little meeting not too long ago and saw the Iron Duke in person.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Seeing him always reminds me of when I first saw the Gastrell.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Like so many other children who grew up hearing tales of the Empire's Death Knell, I searched for the shadow of the ruins that belonged to Lingones, only to find not Gaul...

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: But the glory of the strongest nation of our time, so splendid that I could not bear to turn away.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You want us to believe you care more about Victoria than Gododdin?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Make no mistake, I would never call myself a patriot.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: A duke must always put his dukedom before all else; this is not just a matter of interest, but also a duty, a responsibility.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: But I wonder... what is the difference between Gododdin and Wellington?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Wellington would still be Wellington, with or without Victoria. But what would become of Gododdin, if the light of Victoria went out?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Perhaps it would survive. But things would certainly not get better.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You don't want the Grand Dukes to really divide Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: I'm not the only one.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: You know that.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: As strong as Victoria is, she is not without her rivals. Ursus, Leithanien, Columbia, Sargon... all the ambitious nations of Terra have their eyes on us.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: We need a single, unified voice to bring stability.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: This is why Parliament exists. All the ducal realms will select an appropriate representative... including Windermere.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: This is what the Exemplars mean to Victoria. No soldier who fights for the cause of Victoria will need to fear betrayal again.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: The Speaker of Parliament has always been the king, for the entirety of the role's existence. But that does not mean that he — or she — must sit on the throne.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: And this is what you can mean to all of us, Your Royal Highness Alexandrina. If you are willing.
No one speaks as the duke's words sink in.
Only the crackling of the fire Gododdin lit can be heard.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I have only one question for Your Grace.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If all of this could have waited until after the war—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Then if I refuse now, can my friends and I leave with the Sighs of Kings?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Siege!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Crossbowmen outside!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We're surrounded. Maybe we already were the moment he showed up...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Well, well. First we learn what a 'commitment' is to Caster, now we learn what 'friendship' is to Gododdin.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Friends treat each other as equals, do they not?

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: My offer remains fair.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: At the minimum... I gave this young friend from Gododdin the opportunity to point her piledriver spear at me.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Lost the signal from Drone 6 again... blasted place!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Alright, Balin, Yvres, Viktor. We have to do this manually.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Status reports, everyone?

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: All good here. The beacon's in there and the sensor's running. We're still getting strong interference from the wind and sand. I'm trying to filter out the noise.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Waiting on you now, Viktor!

steps.name: Sniper Operator
steps.text: Five minutes. The ground's softer than expected.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Careful, quicksand!

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: The soil's very different from the samples we collected. I've sent the data back. You got that, captain?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I knew it was a good idea to get you onboard, Yvres. Worth a few days of angry stares from Earthspirit.

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: I think you can do with a better working environment, Closure. Try not to get too much sand in your mouth...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Stop talking like Amiya, Balin!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: My blood is self-cleansing...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Haha.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hey! Don't just laugh at me, keep working! The sooner we get this signal tower set up, the sooner we can broadcast the safe zone locations, and the sooner you can go to town.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I'm trying! Rhodes Island equipment isn't like anything else I've seen. I'm already doing an 'exemplary' job, get it?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Seriously, though. You and Rockrock shouldn't be here with me in the first place.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: You have my drones. Of course I'm staying here with them.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Well, that is a solid reason.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I know you’re concerned about my safety, but I’m actually really strong! What’s that… those Vampire worms would disagree? Well, not all Vampires are built the same, you know?

spans.text: I know you’re concerned about my safety, but I’m actually really strong! What’s that… those Vampire worms would disagree? Well, not
Vampires are built the same, you know?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's you two I'm worried about. Put your helmets on. Oripathy infection is no joke.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Alright, alright. But you lot are the ones who need to be careful, running around the battlefield like this.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: 'You lot'?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Rhodes Island. You lot are all over the battlefield, not caring for your own safety at all.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Balin is an Infected from Victoria. Yvres is Infected, but not Victorian. Viktor isn't Infected or Victorian. How amazing...

spans.text: Balin is an Infected from Victoria. Yvres is Infected, but not Victorian. Viktor isn't Infected

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Why? Everyone knows Rhodes Island operators come from everywhere.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I can't help but think of my Granny, Clovisia... plus Tommy and the gang.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I once hoped that the Self-Salvation Corps could be as united as the Rhodes Island operators I'd seen.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well... people aren't really born good or bad.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: As circumstances change, so do people. Maybe, one day...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: One day, the Self-Salvation Corps will become a tightly knit, united group.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Just like the Exemplars, now all fighting for the same thing. We're ready to brave the worst, ready to deal with defeat, even betrayal.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: But it's not necessarily race, upbringing or circumstance that will unite us... just like Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Alright, alright, enough with the compliments, I know you want to keep our equipment. Should I get you a contract now?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I'm not jealous of Rhodes Island, Miss Closure.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: You lot give me the same kind of feeling as this strange communication equipment you're holding.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: A possibility. Something that proves I'm not just a naive dreamer.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Maybe your monologue is starting to bother Closure, Feist...

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: What's that sound?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Let me check the feed from Rock-18...
In the monitor's pixelated image, a sand storm approaches quickly.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Catastrophe? But I don't see the data...
Beneath the wild sands are tattered banners and the chanting of war.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Nachzehrers... what are they doing here?!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Go.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You two, leave, now. Everyone from the Self-Salvation Corps, head for Gibsonham, now!

steps.name: Victorian Sergeant
steps.text: What's that sound—

steps.name: Victorian Sergeant
steps.text: S-Sarkaz! They're already here!

steps.name: Victorian Sergeant
steps.text: Battle stations! Open fire!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Explosions?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Sir, the Sarkaz are attacking the town! We have to leave, now.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: They found us quicker than expected.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Looks like the Sarkaz remember the success they had with Amphelise.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: What of the attackers?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Nachzehrer elites, sir.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Your Royal Highness, you and your people must leave with us, now. This town is not worth defending, but you and your friends are of paramount importance to the future of Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Our battleships can take us back to the Silverrock Bluffs front in three hours. That is where you belong.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Me or the sword?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Sir, we don't have time—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You don't have time and you don't plan to fight, even though you know how many civilians there are.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But of course you wouldn't. They're not important to you or the Parliament. These poor families wouldn't produce a single member of Parliament in a hundred years.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: There's no place for them in your game of cards.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: I simply have my sights on reality, Your Highness.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Reality? Reality is that the future of Victoria you dream of is to be found in grand halls filled with noble coats of arms.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: My Victoria is here with these people.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Sir—

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Very well, Your Royal Highness.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: You're like your father at times. Naive, reckless...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is that so? Not that I care. I don't remember anything about him.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Hah. Very well.

steps.name: Duke of Gododdin
steps.text: Good luck.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Horn. Order all combat-ready personnel on the plate to their stations, now.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: On it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Delphine. Have Lieutenant Shearer get the logistics and medical staff ready.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Already done.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Follow the plan. Protect the civilians. Prepare for battle!
